taskTitle: NIST SP 800-63B password rules, current revision

checks.detail: 3 subtasks, read from the schema reply
5 phases had the tools designed for them

breakdown.label: topic single-factor-minimum-length: minimum length of a password used as the only authentication factor (characters)
topic maximum-length: the maximum password length verifiers permit (characters)
topic composition-rules: imposing composition rules, such as requiring a mix of character types
topic periodic-change: requiring subscribers to change their passwords periodically
topic password-hints: letting subscribers store a password hint that unauthenticated claimants can see
topic security-questions: prompting for knowledge-based authentication or security questions when a password is chosen
topic blocklist: checking a new password against a blocklist of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords
topic password-managers: allowing password managers and autofill
topic salt-length: the length of the salt used when storing passwords (bits)
topic hashing-scheme: using an approved password hashing scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132

finalText:
All ten requirements come from section 3.1.1.2, "Password Verifiers", of NIST SP 800-63B-4 (Revision 4). The workers read it at https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html, and I rely on their reports only.

- **Which revision is current:** One worker said Revision 4 is the newest revision on the NIST pages site and that Revision 3 turned up in search but was not used. Another worker did not check whether a newer revision exists. None of them opened Revision 3, so I can't say how it differs.
- **Disagreement between workers:** There was none. One worker's window did not reach the salt-length sentence, but the salt worker found it on the same page, so the reports are consistent.
- **Keyword strength:** Three of the ten are weaker than SHALL or SHALL NOT. Maximum length is only a SHOULD, hashing scheme is only a SHOULD, and shorter passwords (at least 8 characters) are allowed as part of multi-factor authentication.
- **Hashing-scheme wording:** The sentence also accepts "updated NIST guidelines on password hashing schemes" as an alternative to SP 800-132. A separate sentence, "Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme", is a SHALL but does not name SP 800-132.
